name: Cable bar curl
cue: Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar to your shoulders.
research: Standing cable curl with a straight bar (20 in, 0.285 H long, 25 mm thick, grips 0.235 H apart, shoulder width, supinated) on a low pulley (0.075 H, in a fork on the column's base) in a column 0.5 H (0.9 m) in front of the stance, feet hip width, knees soft (6). Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial: the elbows stay pinned at the sides (shoulder flexion 9 -> 14, so they drift about 5 deg forward at the top as the upper arm does; abduction about 3), the elbow flexes 12 -> 128 (not fully straight at the bottom so the fists clear the thighs), wrists neutral, trunk still. The hands are fitted so the grip tunnel stays along the left-right axis (sagittal curl, tilt under 0.2 deg) and the bar passes through both fists; the cable is on the middle of the bar and leaves it 51 deg below horizontal at the bottom and 70 deg at the top (the moment arm against the cable, the sine of the angle between the forearm and the cable, is 0.28 of its maximum at the bottom, 0.91 at mid-range and 0.82 at the top). Cable 1:1 to the stack. Geometry: design/cable/bc.mjs.

targets.note: design values (standard technique), not a measured trial

camera.note: The view of the hammer curl (az 60, el 12): the front of the near arm faces the camera, the biceps reads as a band down the front of the upper arm at the bottom and an oval in the crook of the elbow at the top, and the cable shows where the load comes from. fitMachine false: the column may crop at the top.
